feature: Stop/interrupt button — abort the in-flight turn of the viewed project
summary: Add a user-initiated stop path that reuses the existing per-run control.abort() (which SIGKILLs the current turn process via TurnHandle.kill in src/turn.ts:65). SessionManager gains interrupt(projectId?) that marks the run as interrupted and calls control.abort(); the run's promise then resolves through the existing turn_failed branch in runSession (src/failover.ts:186-201, status:'failed', reason:'signal SIGKILL'). Because the manager set an `interrupted` flag on the ActiveRun, launch() emits a NEW `turn_interrupted` event instead of `session_done` (disambiguating a user stop from a genuine failure), still followed by the usual `turn_state{active:false}`. A POST /api/interrupt {projectId?} endpoint mirrors /api/switch. The panel shows a Stop button in place of Send while the viewed project's turn is active, posts to /api/interrupt, and renders a "stopped" banner on turn_interrupted. Next message resumes because lastSessionId is already persisted by saveStateOnce on the first tap event (server/manager.ts:286-294).

Always immediately followed by the existing turn_state{active:false} (also projectId-tagged).

newEndpoints: POST /api/interrupt — body { projectId?: string } (defaults to current project). Returns 200 { interrupted: true } when a run was aborted; throws 409 ConflictException('no session running') when the targeted project has no active run with a control. Auth guard applies like every /api route.

feature: Slash commands in the composer (/clear, /compact, /model, /effort, + discoverable custom project commands)
summary: Add a "/" command menu to the composer that mirrors Claude Code web. Typing "/" as the first token opens a keyboard-navigable popover listing two kinds of commands: UI-local commands that never touch the CLI (/clear = new conversation, /model, /effort, /resume, /switch) and CLI-passthrough commands whose text is sent verbatim as the prompt so the headless `claude -p` interprets them (/compact and any custom `.claude/commands/*.md` for the current project's cwd). Passthrough works today because src/turn.ts:40 already puts `--` before the positional prompt, so a "/"-prefixed prompt reaches the CLI untouched. Custom commands are discovered server-side from the project cwd and returned via a new GET /api/commands. Dispatch is decided at send time by matching against a JS registry: UI-local commands run locally and return without POSTing; everything else flows through the existing send/continue endpoints unchanged. No new SSE events, no new run plumbing, works per-project because the menu is scoped to currentProjectId and passthrough uses the existing projectId-tagged send path.
newEndpoints: GET /api/commands?projectId=<id> — returns ProjectCommand[] (auth-guarded like all /api routes via ApiController). No body. Response: [{name, description, argumentHint?, source:'project'|'user'}]. projectId optional; defaults to the current project.

feature: Per-project message queue: enqueue a message while a turn is busy, auto-send when the turn finishes, with cancel and "interrupt and send now".
summary: Today `POST /api/sessions/current/messages` throws `BusyError` → 409 when a project's turn is running (server/manager.ts:267, api.controller.ts:116). This feature adds a per-project FIFO queue keyed by projectId (mirroring the existing `runs` Map at manager.ts:75). When a project is busy, the continue endpoint enqueues the (already image-composed) prompt + model/effort instead of 409ing; when that project's turn settles, the manager's `.finally` drain (manager.ts:321) pops the next queued message and launches a `--resume` continuation of the just-finished session. A queue_update SSE event (tagged with projectId, like every other event) keeps the panel's queued-chip strip and per-project sidebar badges live across parallel projects. "Interrupt and send now" front-enqueues the message then calls the existing per-run `control.abort()` (manager.ts:395, failover.ts:81) so the drain immediately continues with the new instruction. Cancel removes a not-yet-sent queued message. All queue state is in-memory (lost on restart), consistent with `runs`/`lastResults`.

newEvents.shape: { projectId: string, queued: QueuedPublic[], added?: QueuedPublic, sent?: QueuedPublic, canceled?: string } where QueuedPublic = { id: string, text: string, model?: string, effort?: string, enqueuedAt: string }. Emitted on enqueue (added), drain/auto-send (sent), and cancel (canceled). `queued` is always the full remaining queue for that project.
{ projectId: string }. Emitted by interruptAndSend right before control.abort() so the panel can suppress the resulting 'session_done: failed' banner and show 'interrupted — sending your message'.

newEndpoints: POST /api/sessions/current/messages — UNCHANGED path/body {prompt?,cwd?,model?,effort?,image?,projectId?}; now @HttpCode(200) and returns {sessionId:string} when sent immediately OR {queued:QueuedPublic} when the project was busy (no longer 409s for busy).

POST /api/sessions/current/interrupt — body {prompt?,cwd?,model?,effort?,image?,projectId?}; aborts the running turn and front-enqueues; returns {queued:QueuedPublic}, or {sessionId} if the project was idle.
POST /api/queue/cancel — body {id:string, projectId?:string}; returns {ok:boolean} (false if id not found in that project's queue).
GET /api/queue?projectId=<id> — returns QueuedPublic[] (that project's current queue; defaults to current project).

Add `interface SubmitParams { text:string; prompt:string; cwd?:string; opts?:TurnRunOptions; projectId?:string }`.
- New field beside `runs` (manager.ts:75): `private queues = new Map<string, QueuedInternal[]>();` and a module-level `const pub = (it:QueuedInternal):QueuedPublic => ({ id:it.id, text:it.text, model:it.model, effort:it.effort, enqueuedAt:it.enqueuedAt });`.
- `private enqueue(pid:string, p:SubmitParams, front:boolean):QueuedPublic` — build QueuedInternal with `randomUUID()`; unshift if front else push into `queues.get(pid) ?? []`; set map; `this.emit('queue_update',{projectId:pid, queued:q.map(pub), added:pub(item)})`; return pub(item).
- `submit(p:SubmitParams): {sessionId:string} | {queued:QueuedPublic}` — resolve pid via `p.projectId ?? this.projects().currentId()` (throw 'no project selected' if none); `if (this.runs.has(pid)) return { queued: this.enqueue(pid,p,false) };` else `return { sessionId: this.continueLast(p.prompt, p.opts, pid) };` (reuses existing continueLast at manager.ts:264, which already resolves lastSessionId/cwd and throws 'no previous session' if none).

feature: Auto-resume interrupted turns on ungraceful container restart
summary: On every turn launch, SessionManager writes a per-project "in-flight" marker file under state/inflight/<projectId>.json and deletes it when the run settles (completed/parked/failed/errored) in the existing `.finally()`. Because the SIGTERM/SIGINT handler in manager.ts calls `run.control?.abort()` then `process.exit(130)` synchronously, the `.finally()` never runs on process death, so any marker on disk is definitionally a turn that was mid-flight when the process died ungracefully. At startup (in the constructor, right after `migrateProjects()`), a new `resumeInterrupted()` scans those markers and relaunches each via the existing `launch()` path with `resume=true` and failover's `CONTINUE_PROMPT`, restoring model/effort. A persisted `attempts` counter incremented-and-flushed before each relaunch bounds poison turns (crash loops) to MAX_AUTO_RESUME_ATTEMPTS. Graceful deploys already swap only when idle (deployer.sh `busy()` gate), so no marker exists during a graceful swap and nothing is auto-resumed — the reconciliation is automatic. The panel gains two notice events so the user sees "auto-resumed after restart".

feature: Answer Claude's questions from the UI — detect when a headless turn ends waiting on a user decision, surface it as an interactive "Claude is asking" card with quick-reply option buttons, and route the answer back over the existing --resume continue path (full context preserved).
summary: I tested the real `claude` 2.1.201 binary and proved the hard facts: (1) `--input-format stream-json` with a persistent stdin keeps ONE process alive across turns and preserves full context with no `--resume`, but a message injected while a tool is running is QUEUED to the next turn boundary — it does NOT preempt a running tool (verified: a "CHANGE OF PLAN" sent mid-Bash was only consumed after the sleep chain finished). (2) With `--dangerously-skip-permissions` (the gateway's actual config) permission prompts never occur — the model just proceeds. Without it (`--permission-mode default`) a tool call is auto-DENIED with a synthetic tool_result and the model asks in plain text then ends the turn; there is NO answerable `control_request` over stdout/stdin in `-p` mode. (3) `AskUserQuestion` is NOT in the headless tool list at all (confirmed twice) — the model cannot emit a structured multiple-choice tool_use. Conclusion: the only real "question" surface in this bypass-permissions, respawn-per-turn gateway is the model writing a question in text and ENDING its turn. So the most capable feasible feature is deterministic question detection + one-click reply, built on the untouched existing spawn+`--resume` architecture (zero risk to failover/tests). To make detection reliable rather than a fuzzy heuristic, the gateway appends a tiny ASK-block convention to user prompts; I verified haiku emits exactly `<<<ASK\nquestion: ...\noptions: a | b >>>` and cleanly ends the turn. A trailing-'?' heuristic is the fallback when the model doesn't use the block.

HARD-LIMIT finding (documented, not a bug): true mid-turn answering / AskUserQuestion / answerable permission prompts do NOT exist in `claude -p` mode — AskUserQuestion is absent from the headless tool list, permission requests under bypass never fire and under default are auto-denied with a synthetic tool_result (no control_request on stdio), and stream-json stdin messages are queued to the next turn boundary rather than preempting a running tool. So 'answer mid-turn without ending the turn' is genuinely impossible here; the design answers at the turn boundary the model itself creates by ending its turn.

A more capable variant — adopt `--input-format stream-json` for ONE persistent multi-turn process (proven to preserve context with no --resume) — was investigated and deferred: it would require reworking failover.ts's turn-completion detection (today `result` coincides with process exit; with persistence the process stays alive after `result`), putting the failover state machine and its tests at risk. Not needed since --resume already preserves context for the answer.

Detection runs on `e.result`; if a future CLI truncates the result string the block could be missed — mitigate by ALSO parsing the final assistant text block in tapToEvents if result parsing returns null.
feasibility: confirmed — for the boundary-based design. Verified live against claude 2.1.201: the ASK-block convention is emitted verbatim and cleanly ends the turn (exp4), stream-json input holds context across turns (exp2), permission prompts are auto-denied with no answerable control_request (exp3), and AskUserQuestion is not exposed in headless -p (exp1/exp2 tool lists). What is NOT feasible in -p mode (and therefore explicitly out of scope): answering a question WITHOUT ending the current turn, native permission-prompt approval, and the AskUserQuestion tool. The chosen design needs none of those and touches neither turn.ts nor failover.ts.
